newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WEBB RALLIES TO WIN LPGA SAFECO CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WEBB RALLIES TO WIN LPGA SAFECO CLASSIC.

text.p: Australian Karrie Webb captured the third victory of her rookie season Sunday, rallying past Tammie Green for a two-shot triumph at the $550,000 LPGA Safeco Classic at Meridian Valley Country Club.
The 21-year-old Webb shot a three-under-par 69 for a 72-hole total of 11-under 277 that was two strokes better than three-time champion Patty Sheehan, who managed even-par 72.
The $82,500 first prize nudged Webb past Laura Davies of Britain and into the lead on the LPGA money list with $769,532. Davies, who has 1996 winnings of $764,081, skipped the tournament.
"Laura and I are good friends," said Webb, who became the fifth three-time winner on the LPGA Tour this year and posted her eighth top three finish.
"(The money) is astounding. I don't think it really hit me. I bought a house and a car. I don't know what to do with it. It's sitting in the bank."

Webb started the day in fourth place, four shots behind third-round leader Green. But she was in the clubhouse with a one-shot lead over Green, who double-bogeyed the 18th hole to fall into a third-place tie with Barb Mucha at 280.
Green struggled to a four-over 76, while Mucha shot 70.
Sheehan, the Hall of Famer who won this tournament for the third time last year, also expressed surprise with the finish.
"Coming up 18, I thought I was playing for third," she said. "Suddenly, I'm looking at a birdie and Tammie's looking at a double-bogey, and suddenly, I'm second."
About Webb, Sheehan said: "She's an incredible story. Everyone's talking about Tiger (Woods). I tell you what, not only does Karrie have the best swing on Tour, she's got a great personality."
